questions.question: Explain the difference between weather and climate, and why it is hot near the equator and cold near the poles.
questions.expected_answer: Weather is the condition of the air at a place and time, and it changes daily. Climate is the usual pattern of weather over about thirty years or more. Near the equator, the sun's rays strike the Earth almost straight on, concentrating the heat, so it is hot. Near the poles, the rays arrive at a slant, spread over a larger area and pass through more atmosphere, so it is cold.

questions.question: Compare the climate of a tropical rainforest, a hot desert and a coniferous forest.
questions.expected_answer: A tropical rainforest is hot all year, about twenty-six degrees, with a tiny temperature range and more than two thousand millimetres of rain spread over every month. A hot desert gets less than two hundred and fifty millimetres of rain, with very hot days, cold nights and rare, sudden storms. A coniferous forest has long, freezing winters with snow, short cool summers, a large temperature range and low to moderate precipitation.

questions.question: Explain three ways in which South Africa's democracy protects people's rights.
questions.expected_answer: Citizens elect their government in free and fair elections with a secret ballot, as first happened on the twenty-seventh of April 1994. The Constitution is the highest law, and its Bill of Rights protects everyone's rights, so any law or action that goes against it is invalid. Independent courts, especially the Constitutional Court, make sure everyone is equal before the law, give accused people a fair trial and can strike down unconstitutional laws.
